title: FIREACT: TOWARD LANGUAGE AGENT FINE-TUNING
abstract: This paper explores fine-tuning language models for language agents, which can reason and act. We propose FireAct, a novel approach to fine-tune language models with diverse trajectories from multiple tasks and prompting methods.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex problem. You can use a language model to generate ideas, but it's not perfect. Fine-tuning the model can improve its performance. We'll explore how to do this for language agents that can reason and act.

Think of a language agent like a personal assistant that can help you with tasks. But instead of just generating text, it can interact with the world and learn from its experiences.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
We use a question answering setup with a Google search API to fine-tune language models. The process involves generating trajectories with a large language model, converting them to a suitable format, and fine-tuning a smaller language model.

This approach allows the language agent to learn from its experiences and improve its performance over time.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Our experiments show that fine-tuning language models can significantly improve their performance. For example, fine-tuning Llama2-7B with 500 trajectories generated by GPT-4 leads to a 77% increase in HotpotQA performance.

We also compare the performance of different language models and fine-tuning methods.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Fine-tuning language models for language agents has several benefits, including improved performance, efficiency, and robustness. It also enables the development of more capable and useful language agents that can reason and act.

Our work opens up new research questions and opportunities for further exploration.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our approach, FireAct, is a novel way to fine-tune language models with diverse trajectories from multiple tasks and prompting methods. This allows the language agent to learn from its experiences and improve its performance over time.

We also explore the effects of different fine-tuning methods and data sizes on the performance of language agents.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
We release the FireAct code, data, and model checkpoints to facilitate further research and development. You can try fine-tuning your own language models and exploring the benefits of language agent fine-tuning.

Our work provides a foundation for developing more capable and useful language agents that can reason and act.
